# `Browser.Notification`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Notification — show system notifications over `Ipe.Ffi.Js` ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism spanning BOTH port
directions: outbound `JsCmd`s (`requestPermission` / `notify`) request a
notification operation, and an inbound `JsMsg` carries the permission outcome or
a display acknowledgement. Both cross the same seal codec and fail-closed port
discipline as every other port; there is no second transport.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses
`js-port:notification` (import-derived, keyed on the canonical
`Ipe.Browser.Notification` path prefix via `WebCapability::for_browser_module`,
alias-immune); only the top-level app's `[capabilities] accepts` set can grant it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.Notification.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound
    ADTs and the full `Options` surface (`title` / `body` / `tag`) for a caller
    that needs every knob.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `requestPermission` (a
    `Task Error ()` that succeeds only when the host grants) and `notify` /
    `notifyWith` (fire a notification), plus `outcomes` — the inbound
    subscription that folds the narrow `JsMsg` into a typed `Result Error ()`.
    The inbound `case` is EXHAUSTIVE over `Granted` / `Denied` / `Shown` /
    `Unavailable`: a host permission denial becomes a typed `Err`, never a
    silently dropped variant.

## `requestPermission`

```ipe
requestPermission : Task Error ()
```

`requestPermission` — ask the host to grant notification permission, as a
`Task Error ()`.

Uses the correlated port→Task bridge (`Js.request`). The served JS handler
calls `Notification.requestPermission`; a grant resolves the `Task` with `()`,
and a denial or an absent API resolves it to a typed `Err`.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:notification`; the app must grant it
with `accepts = [ JsPort Notification ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `notify`

```ipe
notify : String -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`notify title` — display a notification with the given title and no body.

Outbound `Cmd`. The served JS handler constructs a `Notification`; a host
denial (no prior grant) or an absent API traps to a typed inbound result on the
`outcomes` subscription, never a panic.

## `notifyWith`

```ipe
notifyWith : Internals.Options -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`notifyWith options` — display a notification with the full option surface
(`title` / `body` / `tag`).

## `outcomes`

```ipe
outcomes : (Result Error () -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`outcomes toMsg` — the inbound subscription, wired in `subscriptions`.

The decoder IS the security gate: every inbound value runs through the total,
bounded seal decoder for the narrow `JsMsg`; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is folded EXHAUSTIVELY into a
`Result Error ()` — a `Granted` / `Shown` becomes `Ok`, a denial becomes a
typed `Err`.
